parsed.explanation: The combined regime is nationally hostile in climate but does not document criminalisation of trans identity or systematic denial of entry. The clearest visitor-facing exposure is derisive, intrusive border questioning of a visibly trans traveller with no recourse. National censorship bans public rainbow expression and LGBT content, LGBTI organising is barred, and no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection exists. Care access is heavily gated and medication import/purchase restricted. Subnational variation is procedural and resident-facing. A successful conversion-treatment lawsuit shows narrow remedies, but not working protection at the border or in public expression. No trans-specific violence rate or custodial targeting is documented; that absence is not safety, but it keeps severity below imprisonment or organised-targeting tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: May 2025 trans visitor was mocked, laughed at and questioned by immigration officials; visibly trans travellers should expect intrusive, derisive handling.
entry_documents.interaction: Border encounter can out the traveller and set tone for the visit; document-marker rules remain unresolved.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No trans-specific arrest, detention or custody placement practice is documented for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border questioning did not reportedly escalate to custody; unknown in other encounters.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Resident-facing sex-segregated enrolment, uniforms, bathrooms, dormitories and conscription are tied to legal marker; no visitor facility rule is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National censorship baseline applies across venues, but no trans-specific visitor facility ban is shown.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care is heavily gated; adults need parental consent for surgery and marker change; online estradiol/antiandrogens banned; conversion practices remain routine.
care_services.protection: One trans person won a record payout against electroshock conversion treatment; youth clinics and expert consensus exist.
care_services.interaction: Short-stay visitors needing HRT may face in-person purchase barriers; emergency care exposure not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State censors LGBT content and public expression; rainbow flags banned even indoors; LGBTI organisations cannot register; no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Narrow court remedy in conversion case only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility raises outing consequences and chills help-seeking; no evidence of police sweeps targeting trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors face parental-consent gates for gender-affirming care and marker change; only one province allows minors to apply for marker change.
minors_guardians.protection: Seven youth clinics, three offering puberty suppression; national expert consensus recommends blockers.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian may face care denial and document friction; visitor-specific practice not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A 2018 rainbow-badge attack by security guards is documented; no trans-specific violence rate or pattern is available.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Security company dismissed the three guards involved.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Single incident cannot establish rate; official response was punitive but not a trans-specific protection regime.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No border complaint recourse; notaries can refuse or impose discriminatory conditions on same-sex guardianship; censorship limits advocacy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts exist and one conversion-treatment payout succeeded.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are narrow and resident-facing; they do not reliably reach border harassment or public-expression censorship.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has routine universal visitor exclusion and seizure at the border with no effective remedy. This dossier documents derisive border questioning but not routine denial or removal, so it sits somewhat above that anchor, while its broad expression censorship and absent protections keep it close.

0.55-B documents systematic secondary screening, discretionary refusal and administrative return. This dossier shows a direct but not yet systematic border-harassment incident, plus stronger national censorship and no equality law; comparable or slightly lower, because entry refusal is less documented but state hostility is broader.

0.75-C has trained border officers, appeal rights, release and compensation. This dossier has none of those operating protections at the border and adds censorship of public gender-nonconforming expression, so it is materially below.

parsed.synthesis: National rules and climate dominate: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection, no registered LGBTI advocacy, censored public expression, gated care and conversion practices. The visitor-specific harm is a documented border encounter with mockery and questioning and no remedy. Subnational variation is procedural and does not mitigate visitor exposure. No criminalisation of trans identity, organised targeting, or custodial placement practice is documented, so the rating stays in the elevated band rather than severe risk.
